questions.q: Why can't summarize count() with no time boundary run against a live, infinite stream the same way it runs against a finite table?
options: It works exactly the same way, there's no difference
KQL doesn't support summarize on streaming data at all
summarize only works on batch-ingested data
The stream never ends, so an unbounded aggregation would keep growing forever and never actually finish computing
questions.explain: A finite table's summarize runs once and finishes; a stream has no end to reach.

questions.q: What is a window, in streaming terms?
options: A Power BI report page
A Fabric workspace UI panel
A KQL Database's storage partition
A time-bounded slice of a stream — a boundary marking where one aggregation bucket ends and the next begins
questions.explain: It's the mechanism that turns an infinite stream into finite, closeable aggregation buckets.

questions.q: What's the difference between event time and processing time?
options: Event time is when something actually happened at the source; processing time is when the system received or processed it
Event time only applies to batch data
They always mean the same timestamp
Processing time is set manually by the developer
questions.explain: Network delays and out-of-order delivery mean these two are almost never identical in a real system.

questions.q: Which upcoming lesson covers windows that overlap, so one event can land in more than one window?
options: Lesson 30, Tumbling windows
Lesson 31, Hopping / Sliding windows
Lesson 26, KQL time series functions
Lesson 32, Session windows
questions.explain: Hopping/sliding windows are fixed-size but overlapping, unlike tumbling windows which are back-to-back and non-overlapping.

questions.q: Why does Databricks & Delta Lake's Structured Streaming (Lesson 33 of that course) use nearly identical windowing vocabulary to Fabric's real-time tools?
options: It's a coincidence with no underlying reason
Because they're built on the exact same codebase
Because Fabric copied Databricks's exact KQL syntax
Because the underlying problem — infinite input, finite output — is the same regardless of engine
questions.explain: Every streaming system needs some concept of a window, because the aggregation problem itself doesn't change by engine.
